environment.description: Service runs behind an internal NLB (Network Load Balancer) in AWS VPC subnet 10.200.0.0/16. The NLB target group has proxy_protocol_v2 enabled but the critical control is at the VPC level: Security Group sg-0a3f8e2c1b (attached to the NLB ENIs) has inbound rules allowing TCP/443 ONLY from three specific CIDR blocks representing corporate office egress IPs (203.0.113.0/28, 198.51.100.64/28, 192.0.2.128/28). Additionally, the VPC has no Internet Gateway route for the subnet hosting the service pods (subnet-0xdeadbeef is in a private subnet with only NAT gateway egress). The NLB itself is scheme=internal. DNS resolution for the service endpoint (chat.internal.corp.example.com) is only available via Route53 private hosted zone associated with the VPC. There is no public DNS record. The combination means: no internet-routable path exists to reach the WebSocket endpoint, and even within AWS, only traffic from the three corporate CIDR ranges can reach the NLB listener.

config.vpc_routing: no IGW attached to service subnet, NAT-gw egress only
config.dns: Route53 private hosted zone, no public record
config.tls_termination: NLB with ACM certificate, TLS 1.2+ only
